title: BER: Add the length check of dissecting BER integers, int64, and booleans
description:
Add the length check of dissecting BER integers, int64, and booleans, the expert info is added for bad lengths, includes the name of the field and actual length.
Related to #18005

If you're checking the length of a boolean (which the code currently doesn't), you might as well test that the length is exactly 1. From X.690:

> 8.2 Encoding of a boolean value

> 8.2.1 The encoding of a boolean value shall be primitive. The contents octets shall consist of a single octet.
Thanks for reviewing the code. You're right, i'll fix it right away.

changed this line in [version 7 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/6524/diffs?diff_id=371452778&start_sha=669e8b7ebee7827afecf52662d8562fe3510a33f#283a7e2df4333e1d492a1af4d6fd943bc1ea90a1_2049_2049)
Boolean length is fixed to 1,only need to check whether the value is 1. fixed.

Please change the commit message to something that describes what's going on a bit more clearly. This may be related to something you have seen in GOOSE, but the behavior change is not limited to that.

You are changing the behavior of dissecting BER integers, int64, and booleans so that expert info is added for bad lengths, including with implicit tags, and so that the expert info includes the name of the field (instead of having more generic error messages about running off the end of the buffer), correct?
Ok,i will describe the commit message more clearly.
